summary: An unwatched acetylene beacon from 1908; the first keeper came with the 1957 station, still staffed on Discovery Passage.

structures.type: steel cylindrical tank on steel framework (acetylene, unwatched)

staffing.basis: Listed as a staffed lightstation with two permanent positions in the Senate committee's 2010 appendix; LighthouseFriends says the station is still staffed (undated).

access.note: Staffed lightstation: the keepers' home and workplace, owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. Land access is over a private logging road. Grounds and tower are closed. Visitors should not land uninvited.

events.note: Acetylene beacon: LighthouseFriends dates the first light to 1908. The report published 1908 already lists the beacon; the report published 1909 lists it as placed in service since the previous report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1957 first-light date (Wikidata) and its 1908 date (Rowlett) describe different things. LighthouseFriends dates the first light to 1908. The 1908 Marine report already lists the beacon, while the 1909 report lists it among gas beacons placed in service since the 1908 report, so the Marine dates do not agree. The 1957 date marks the staffed station with its fog horn and dwellings (LighthouseFriends).
The Coast Guard list position, 50°20'00.6" N 125°26'25.9" W, matches the OSM point within a few metres. The Wikidata point lies about 500 m east of it and should not be used.
The 1908 Marine report describes a masonry base; LighthouseFriends describes a concrete base. The sources differ and the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the only roster is LighthouseFriends' list of keepers (no USLHS roster exists for Canada). Its names after about 1960 are used only as the page prints them, in public role; the story names none of them except in the roster. The 2012 rescue comes only from a keeper's own account printed on LighthouseFriends, and the Coast Guard's record of it was not read. Current staffing is not confirmed from a source read here: the 2010 Senate appendix and LighthouseFriends' undated 'still staffed' are the basis; the Coast Guard's 31 July 2024 release named in the record was not read, so check it before publication. The record's 'tower built 1908' describes a steel tank on framework; the present tower's date is not given in any source read. The 1908 and 1910 Marine volumes are cited by session year because the OCR of their titles is garbled. Vancouver's journal was not read directly; his wording is taken as LighthouseFriends quotes it. Rowlett's Lighthouse Directory and Wikidata were not read directly. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1909 Marine report's list of gas beacons placed in service since the last report (printed p. 91, scan p. 100; page image viewed) includes Chatham Point, while the 1908 report's beacon inventory already names it; the story reports both and does not settle the year beyond LighthouseFriends' 1908. The Coast Guard List of Lights entry (No. 518) was checked against the story: Fl G 5s, 6.4 m above water, 8 NM, fog horn blast 2 s, silent 18 s. The 2012 rescue rests on the keeper's account printed on LighthouseFriends; the story gives it as the keeper's account and does not add detail beyond it.
